title: Can you connect jobs and data?

questions.prompt: A workflow has test and lint jobs with no needs keys. What should you expect?

options.label: GitHub may run them in parallel
GitHub must run them in the order written
GitHub must place both on the same runner

questions.explanation: Jobs are independent by default, so GitHub may schedule them concurrently on separate runners.

questions.prompt: Order the dependency flow for a workflow where deployment requires both tests and linting.

options.label: The workflow starts test and lint independently
Both test and lint complete successfully
The deploy job with needs: [test, lint] starts

questions.explanation: Independent checks can fan out, while needs creates the join that deployment must wait for.

questions.prompt: Which data choices fit their stated purpose? Select all that apply.

options.label: Use a job output for a small version string needed by another job
Use an artifact for built files needed by a later job
Use a cache to speed repeated dependency installation
Use a cache as the durable record of released files

questions.explanation: Outputs carry small values, artifacts preserve files, and caches accelerate recomputation. A cache is not durable result storage.

questions.prompt: When is a matrix a good fit?

options.label: The same test steps must run against Node 22 and Node 24
Three unrelated jobs need entirely different commands
An operator must type a deployment approval

questions.explanation: A matrix expands one stable job definition across systematic input variants such as runtime versions or operating systems.

questions.prompt: Design a build and deploy flow that passes version 1.4.0 and a dist directory from one job to another.
questions.rubric: Credit answers that make deploy depend on build, expose the version as a job output, upload dist as an artifact in build, and download that artifact in deploy. The answer should not assume a shared filesystem.
questions.reference_answer: The build job creates dist, writes 1.4.0 as a step output, maps it to a job output, and uploads dist as an artifact. The deploy job declares needs: build, reads the version through needs.build.outputs, and downloads the artifact before publishing it.
questions.explanation: Small values and files cross job boundaries through explicit mechanisms because the two jobs may run on different machines.

questions.prompt: A teammate wants the deploy job to retrieve the exact site produced by build. Which mechanism should hold the site?
questions.explanation: An artifact transfers and preserves the exact build files. A cache is an optimization and a same-job environment variable cannot hold a directory for another job.

questions.prompt: Jobs without needs may run {{job-timing}}. Use a {{small-value}} for a version string, an {{exact-files}} for built files, and a {{recompute-speed}} to speed repeated dependency work.
questions.explanation: Independent jobs may run in parallel. Outputs carry small values, artifacts carry exact files, and caches reduce repeated work.
